papers.title: Differential evolution of neuroinflammatory remodeling programs related to scar formation and regeneration in spinal cord injury: A cross-species multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: Spinal cord injury in mammals often transitions from an acute inflammatory response to persistent neuroinflammatory and scar-associated remodeling, whereas zebrafish attenuate injury-induced inflammatory programs during regenerative repair. The molecular programs underlying these divergent outcomes remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated phase-aligned mouse and zebrafish spinal cord injury datasets using single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, pathway and regulon analyses, expression-based ligand-receptor co-expression analysis, machine-lea
papers.summary: This study integrates phase-aligned mouse and zebrafish spinal cord injury datasets using single-cell/single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics to compare how neuroinflammatory and scar-associated remodeling programs diverge across species. The authors identify molecular programs, regulons, and ligand-receptor interactions that distinguish persistent mammalian scarring from zebrafish regenerative repair, highlighting cross-species differences in inflammatory resolution.

papers.title: Decoding spatial mTOR signalling reveals distinct roles in the tumour microenvironment.
papers.abstract: The tumour microenvironment comprises a variety of cell types that interact with malignant cells, influencing both cancer progression and the patient response to therapy. Given the intricate interactions among these components, assessing how signalling pathways contribute to cancer progression by acting on different components of the TME is particularly complex. Multiplexed imaging allows simultaneous assessment of signalling in multiple of these components. Here, we utilise a highly multiplexed dataset of 61 markers across 746 colorectal tumours to investigate how complex mTOR signalling in d
papers.summary: This study uses highly multiplexed imaging of 61 markers across 746 colorectal tumours to map mTOR signalling activity in different cell types within the tumour microenvironment. The analysis reveals that mTOR signalling plays distinct, cell-type-specific roles in shaping cancer progression and therapy response, demonstrating the value of spatial profiling for disentangling complex signalling in heterogeneous tissues.

papers.title: Lossless compression of protein databases for efficient and accurate metagenomic sequence classification with Centrifuger.
papers.abstract: We present a lossless compression algorithm for indexing a protein database while supporting fast taxonomic classification in the method Centrifuger. The algorithm is a new scheme of the previously proposed run-block compression algorithm to reduce the size of the Ferragina-Manzini (FM) index, and it scales better with alphabet size than the original. On the RefSeq prokaryotic and viral protein sequences, Centrifuger reduces the memory footprint by over a third compared to the method Kaiju that builds on a plain FM-index, while having comparable running time. Furthermore, the compressed FM-ind
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Centrifuger introduces a lossless compression algorithm for protein database indexes that shrinks the Ferragina-Manzini (FM) index using a new run-block compression scheme that scales better with alphabet size. On RefSeq prokaryotic and viral protein sequences, it reduces memory footprint by over a third compared to Kaiju while maintaining comparable running time, enabling efficient and accurate metagenomic sequence classification.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and computational pathology analyses reveal a C11orf24-associated stem-like epithelial population linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune evasion in bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: Cancer stem-like cells drive tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epithelial stemness hierarchy in bladder cancer (BLCA) remains poorly defined. We aimed to characterize stemness-associated epithelial populations and their clinical significance.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell transcriptomics with computational pathology to identify a stem-like epithelial population in bladder cancer marked by C11orf24. This population is associated with remodeling of the tumor microenvironment and immune evasion, and the authors link it to clinical outcomes. The work helps define the epithelial stemness hierarchy in bladder cancer and highlights a candidate marker for further study.

papers.title: A multi-omics study integrating single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and mendelian randomization unveil the implication of TRDMT1 expression in T cells on the immunotherapeutic response and prognosis in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: m5C, an important RNA modification, is closely associated with breast cancer; however, their causal relationship is unknown. We examined the relationship between m5C regulation and breast cancer. Genome-wide association study breast cancer data and expression quantitative trait loci of m5C regulatory factor genes in blood were collected. We explored the causal relationship among m5C regulatory genes, breast cancer susceptibility, and prognosis through Mendelian randomization. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from peripheral blood mononuclear cells of patients with breast cancer and healthy cont
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with Mendelian randomization to investigate how m5C RNA modification regulators, particularly TRDMT1, influence breast cancer susceptibility, prognosis, and immunotherapy response. The authors identify TRDMT1 expression in T cells as a potential causal factor affecting immunotherapeutic outcomes, linking an RNA modification to clinical breast cancer phenotypes.

papers.title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell-to-bulk transcriptome mapping.
papers.abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug se
papers.summary: The authors present CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that first deconvolves bulk RNA-seq data into cell-type composition and cell-type-specific expression, then uses this to resolve bulk drug sensitivity signals. This allows drug response measured in heterogeneous tissue samples to be attributed to specific cell populations rather than treated as an aggregate.

papers.title: CDState Resolves Malignant Cell Heterogeneity from Bulk Tumor RNA Sequencing Data.
papers.abstract: Intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity (ITTH), defined as the coexistence of diverse cell states within a single tumor, complicates cancer treatment and contributes to variable therapeutic responses. Although single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) can resolve this complexity, its cost and technical demands limit large-scale use. Bulk RNA-seq provides a scalable alternative but requires computational methods to deconvolve bulk transcriptomes into distinct cell states. Existing supervised approaches rely on accurate reference data, which are lacking for many cancer types, whereas unsupervised
papers.summary: CDState is a computational method that deconvolves bulk tumor RNA sequencing data into distinct malignant cell states, addressing intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity without requiring reference datasets. Unlike supervised approaches that depend on accurate single-cell references (often unavailable for many cancer types), this unsupervised method offers a scalable alternative to scRNA-seq for resolving cell-state complexity. This could enable large-scale studies of tumor heterogeneity and its role in variable therapeutic responses.

papers.title: Donor-aware integration of public single-cell and spatial transcriptomes identifies a VIC remodeling program and FN1-NT5E spatial association in calcific aortic valve disease.
papers.abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) involves interacting endothelial, interstitial, immune and extracellular-matrix programs, but public single-cell studies contain many cells and few donors. A staged, donor-aware computational workflow was applied to five public human transcriptomic datasets. GSE220774 was used for single-cell discovery; GSE51472, GSE194180 and GSE235995 for fixed-signature replication; and GSE306288 for donor-level spatial assessment. Donors or patients, rather than cells or spots, were treated as biological replicates. VIC9 ranked highest for a prespecified fibrocalcific c
papers.summary: This study applies a donor-aware computational workflow to five public human transcriptomic datasets to study calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD), treating donors rather than individual cells or spots as biological replicates to avoid pseudoreplication. The authors identify a valvular interstitial cell (VIC) remodeling program (VIC9) and a spatial association between FN1 and NT5E in CAVD tissue. The work highlights the importance of donor-level analysis in single-cell and spatial studies where many cells come from few donors.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19.
papers.abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartme
papers.summary: Using Visium spatial transcriptomics on lung tissue from fatal COVID-19 cases and controls, this study maps how cell composition and gene expression change across progressive stages of diffuse alveolar damage. The authors report a progressive loss of endothelial cells, type I pneumocytes, and natural killer cells, alongside an increase in myeloid and stromal cells (especially peribronchial fibroblasts) as disease advances from acute to proliferative DAD. Spatial analysis further identifies distinct tissue compartments with specific cellular and molecular signatures.

papers.title: Cellular scaling laws in the mammalian brain.
papers.abstract: Recent whole-brain cell atlases have uncovered a consistent cytoarchitectural feature: the greatest diversity of discrete neuronal cell types resides not in the regions with the most neurons (e.g., the cortex and cerebellum) but rather in deep subcortical structures like the hypothalamus and brain stem. We propose that this discrepancy reflects a fundamental algorithmic division in the vertebrate brain between a "learning subsystem" and a "steering subsystem." The learning subsystem (cortex, striatum, and cerebellum) scales via the replication of repetitive modules to maximize computational ca
papers.summary: The paper proposes that whole-brain cell atlases reveal a consistent pattern: the greatest diversity of neuronal cell types is found in deep subcortical regions like the hypothalamus and brain stem, not in neuron-rich areas like the cortex and cerebellum. The authors interpret this as evidence for two distinct subsystems in the vertebrate brain—a "learning subsystem" (cortex, striatum, cerebellum) that scales by replicating repetitive modules, and a "steering subsystem" with high cell-type diversity in subcortical structures.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal a DLL4-associated tip-like endothelial niche linked to neoadjuvant chemotherapy non-response in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy non-response remains a major challenge in bladder cancer, yet the endothelial states and intercellular communication programs associated with treatment failure remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomic data, computational analyses, and in vitro experiments to characterize endothelial programs associated with chemotherapy response. A non-response-related transcriptional program was preferentially enriched in endothelial cells and was most prominent in the TipEC_2 tip-like endothelial subset. Integrative an
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk transcriptomics to identify endothelial cell states associated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy non-response in muscle-invasive bladder cancer. The authors find that a non-response-associated transcriptional program is enriched in endothelial cells, particularly a tip-like endothelial subset (TipEC_2) marked by DLL4, suggesting this vascular niche may contribute to treatment failure. In vitro experiments support the computational findings.

papers.title: The gene expression signature of multinucleated giant cells in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice.
papers.abstract: Multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) are associated with chronic inflammation and infectious diseases, but their biological characteristics in vivo remain poorly understood because intact cells are difficult to isolate from tissues. In visceral leishmaniasis, heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs are observed in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice, suggesting that these cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. In this study, we established a method for isolating intact MGCs from the spleens of chronically infected BALB/c mice and performed transcriptomic
papers.summary: The authors developed a method to isolate intact multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) from the spleens of mice chronically infected with Leishmania donovani, a parasite causing visceral leishmaniasis. They then profiled the transcriptome of these cells, which are heavily parasitized and hemophagocytic, to characterize their gene expression signature. This provides the first in vivo molecular characterization of MGCs in this infection context, offering insight into their potential role in parasite persistence and disease pathology.

papers.title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated risk program for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary metastasis/relapse (PM/R) is a major cause of osteosarcoma treatment failure. We aimed to develop a compact transcriptomic PM/R risk score and characterize associated immune and single-cell programs.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to build a compact risk score for pulmonary metastasis or relapse in osteosarcoma, centered on a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated program. The score stratifies patients by metastatic/relapse risk and links high risk to suppressed immune features, with single-cell analysis characterizing the associated cellular programs.

papers.title: Single-cell, spatial, and machine learning analyses identify ANKIB1 as an oligodendrocyte-anchored palmitoylation-associated candidate biomarker of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive neurodegeneration and cognitive decline, yet most candidate therapies targeting amyloid-β have failed to robustly modify disease progression, underscoring an incomplete mechanistic understanding. Oligodendrocytes (ODCs) have recently emerged as active contributors to AD pathology, but the cell-type-specific role of protein S-palmitoylation - a reversible lipid post-translational modification regulating membrane targeting and trafficking - in AD remains uncharacterized. Here we performed an integrated multi-omics analysis combining single
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with machine learning to identify ANKIB1 as an oligodendrocyte-specific, palmitoylation-associated candidate biomarker for Alzheimer's disease. The work highlights a previously underappreciated role for oligodendrocytes and protein S-palmitoylation in AD pathology, offering a new candidate target beyond amyloid-β.

papers.title: TRIM29 may facilitate progression of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma through immune remodeling.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy characterized by late diagnosis, aggressive progression, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Biomarkers with both diagnostic value and biological relevance remain urgently needed.
papers.journal: Pancreatology : official journal of the International Association of Pancreatology (IAP) ... [et al.]
papers.summary: This study investigates TRIM29 as a potential biomarker and driver of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma progression, focusing on its role in remodeling the immune microenvironment. The authors propose that TRIM29 may promote tumor progression through immune modulation, though the abstract provides limited detail on the specific mechanisms or validation approaches.

papers.title: A cellular view of seed development and germination.
papers.abstract: Seeds are fundamental to global food security, yet their encapsulated structure, dense storage compounds, and spatial heterogeneity have created a "hidden box" problem, often restricting research to bulk and tissue approaches that mask cell type-specific regulatory programs. Advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics now enable systematic dissection of seed biology at cellular resolution. This review provides a cellular view spanning the developmental continuum from fertilization to seedling establishment by synthesizing single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies in Arabidopsis th
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent single-cell and spatial transcriptomics studies of seed biology, primarily in Arabidopsis, to overcome the limitations of bulk and tissue-level approaches that obscure cell type-specific regulatory programs. It presents a cellular-resolution view spanning the entire continuum from fertilization through seed development to germination and seedling establishment.

papers.title: CABOPRE: Evaluating Perioperative Cabozantinib's Efficacy and Biomarkers for Cytoreductive Nephrectomy in Advanced Renal Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Despite advances in metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC), long-term survival is poor and biomarkers are lacking. Optimal integration of cytoreductive nephrectomy (CN) in the current era remains controversial. CABOPRE, the first phase II trial assessing perioperative cabozantinib in mRCC patients eligible for CN, aimed to determine its effects in this setting, integrating tumor outcomes with molecular profiling.
papers.summary: CABOPRE is the first phase II trial testing perioperative cabozantinib in metastatic renal cell carcinoma patients undergoing cytoreductive nephrectomy, aiming to assess efficacy and identify biomarkers by integrating tumor outcomes with molecular profiling. The abstract describes the trial's rationale and design rather than reporting results, highlighting the need for better biomarkers and clarification of nephrectomy's role in the current treatment era.

papers.title: NoiBic: a noise-tolerant biclustering algorithm for high-throughput gene expression data analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput transcriptomic technologies generate large-scale gene expression datasets for functional module discovery. However, technical and biological noise can obscure coherent expression patterns and compromise module detection. Noise-tolerant methods are therefore needed to recover meaningful biclusters.
papers.summary: The authors present NoiBic, a biclustering algorithm designed to tolerate noise in high-throughput gene expression data. It aims to recover coherent gene-condition modules that would otherwise be obscured by technical and biological noise, improving functional module discovery from transcriptomic datasets.

papers.title: PRISM-GEP: Viewing single-cell expression through the lens of topic modeling.
papers.abstract: Gene-expression programs (GEPs) are the co-regulated gene modules whose coordinated activity encodes biological processes. Recovering them from single-cell RNA-seq is hard because regulation is many-to-many. A cell can run several programs at once, and a gene can take part in several. Methods that resolve programs along a trajectory break this structure by assigning each gene to a single program.
papers.summary: PRISM-GEP applies topic modeling to single-cell RNA-seq data to recover gene-expression programs (co-regulated gene modules) without forcing each gene into a single program, preserving the many-to-many structure between genes and programs. This addresses a key limitation of trajectory-based methods that assign each gene to one program, allowing cells to run multiple programs simultaneously.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of CARGs is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using Seurat, and CARG activi
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from GEO to characterize cell adhesion-related gene (CARG) expression in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors identify CARG signatures associated with inflammatory infiltration and blood-brain barrier disruption, proposing them as candidate therapeutic targets. The work is primarily descriptive and relies on public data, with limited experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing data with machine learning to characterize the ovarian cancer microenvironment after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The authors identify chronic inflammation signatures and specific cancer-associated fibroblast subsets that are enriched in residual disease and associated with poor clinical outcomes. These findings suggest that targeting these fibroblast populations and inflammatory programs could improve treatment strategies for ovarian cancer.

papers.title: Pasta, a Versatile Transcriptomic Clock, Maps the Chemical and Genetic Determinants of Aging and Rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: With the growing burden of age-related diseases, understanding and modulating the aging process has become a priority. Transcriptomic aging clocks (TACs) can track biological age but remain limited by platform dependence, tissue specificity, or restricted accessibility. To address this, we developed Pasta, a robust and broadly applicable human TAC, built using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework. Pasta accurately predicted relative age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq as well as microarray data. Its predictions aligned with senescent and stem-lik
papers.summary: The authors developed Pasta, a transcriptomic aging clock trained with a novel 'age-shift' learning framework that predicts relative biological age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-seq and microarray data. Pasta's predictions aligned with senescence and stem-like states, and the clock was used to map chemical and genetic determinants of aging and rejuvenation. This provides a versatile, platform-independent tool for studying aging biology.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial biology approaches, particularly spatial transcriptomics, are being applied to cancer epigenetics to study how local tissue context shapes regulatory programs in tumors. It argues that while bulk and single-cell sequencing have advanced tumor biology, they lose spatial information, and integrating spatial methods with epigenetic profiling is needed to understand microenvironmental organization and cell-cell communication.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: The authors developed a gentle hydrogen peroxide bleaching method that removes melanin pigment while preserving tissue for immunohistochemistry, allowing them to track the development of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye on a unified timeline. They combined this with marker staining (Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp, S100b, Cd34, Dct/Tyrp2) and reanalysis of published single-cell RNA-seq data to build a developmental atlas of pigmented ocular tissues. This provides a practical methodological advance and a reference resource for studying eye pigmentation and development.

papers.title: Condition-Associated Pattern Extraction and Recovery From Multi-Condition Single-Cell RNA-seq Data With CAPER.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in multi-condition single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data analysis is the disentanglement of true biological signals from unwanted variations in complex experimental designs. Current statistical and machine learning-based methods struggle with this task, often providing only visualizable embeddings, over-correcting and discarding biological signal, or failing to resolve cell-type-specific responses. Here, we present CAPER, a matrix factorization framework that explicitly disentangles shared biological states from condition-specific variations. CAPER directly outputs an
papers.summary: CAPER is a matrix factorization framework for multi-condition single-cell RNA-seq data that explicitly separates shared biological states from condition-specific variation, rather than only producing visual embeddings like many existing methods. It aims to avoid the common pitfalls of over-correction (losing real biology) and failure to resolve cell-type-specific responses to conditions. The tool directly outputs interpretable condition-associated patterns that can be recovered and analyzed.

papers.title: Normalization choice drives biological interpretation in single-cell RNA-seq cancer studies: A systematic benchmarking of 465 computational pipelines.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed our understanding of tumor heterogeneity, yet the impact of computational pipeline choices on biological conclusions remains poorly characterized. Here, we systematically benchmark 465 combinations of 5 normalization methods and 4 clustering algorithms across 3 cancer datasets encompassing over 434,000 cells. We introduce the Biological Discordance Score (BDS), a metric that quantifies how marker gene interpretation changes across pipelines. We find that normalization method choice has a greater impact on biological interpretation than clu
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 465 computational pipelines combining 5 normalization methods and 4 clustering algorithms across 3 cancer scRNA-seq datasets (>434,000 cells). The authors introduce a Biological Discordance Score (BDS) to quantify how marker gene interpretation shifts across pipelines, and find that normalization choice affects biological interpretation more than clustering algorithm choice. The work highlights that computational pipeline decisions can materially change conclusions drawn from single-cell cancer studies.

papers.title: Molecular traces of microbial cross-kingdom migration: from the gut ecosystem to the intervertebral disc microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Low back pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is strongly associated with its development. Recent studies have shown that the gut microbiota (GM) and its metabolites may be involved in the occurrence and development of IVDD through the gut-disc axis. However, the key microbes mediating this process and their specific molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
papers.summary: This paper investigates the 'gut-disc axis' hypothesis, proposing that gut microbes and their metabolites migrate to intervertebral discs and contribute to disc degeneration, a major cause of low back pain. The authors aim to identify the specific microbial species and molecular mechanisms involved in this cross-kingdom migration from the gut ecosystem to the disc microenvironment.

papers.title: Integrated Spatial and Bulk Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Multicellular Ecosystem Involved in Progression of Young Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Young breast cancer (YBC), defined as diagnosis at or before the age of 40 years, is characterized by an aggressive phenotype and poor prognosis. The tumor microenvironment (TME), comprising immune and stromal cells, plays a critical role in tumor initiation and progression and is closely associated with clinical outcomes. However, alterations in cell states and the organization of multicellular ecosystems within the YBC microenvironment remain poorly understood. We analyzed 7379 bulk transcriptome samples and spatial transcriptomic data from eight samples using EcoTyper and complementary spat
papers.summary: This study combined bulk transcriptomic data from 7,379 samples with spatial transcriptomic data from eight young breast cancer (YBC) tumors to characterize the tumor microenvironment. Using EcoTyper and complementary spatial analyses, the authors identified a multicellular ecosystem—comprising specific immune and stromal cell states—associated with YBC progression and poor prognosis. The work highlights how cell-state organization, not just cell-type composition, contributes to the aggressive phenotype of breast cancer in young women.

papers.title: Spatial and Single-Cell Multi-Omics Analyses of T-Cell Subsets and Interactions in Melanoma Lymph Node Metastasis.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is a highly immunogenic malignancy, yet responses to systemic therapy remain variable. The tumour-draining lymph node (TDLN), including the sentinel lymph node (SLN) during early regional spread, is not only a site of metastatic dissemination but also an important setting for T-cell priming and immune regulation. Conventional classification of nodes as tumour-positive or tumour-negative provides essential staging information but reveals little about their immune state. Single-cell immune transcriptomics, T-cell receptor sequencing and single-cell epigenomics now allow T-cell states, c
papers.summary: This study uses spatial and single-cell multi-omics (immune transcriptomics, TCR sequencing, and epigenomics) to characterize T-cell subsets and their interactions in melanoma tumor-draining lymph nodes, including sentinel nodes during early metastasis. The work moves beyond the binary tumor-positive/negative staging to reveal immune states and T-cell priming/regulation within the TDLN. It provides a detailed map of T-cell states and interactions that may help explain variable responses to systemic immunotherapy.

papers.title: Multi-omics integration and machine learning identify an ACKR1+ endothelial cell-based lactate-immune signature associated with carotid plaque vulnerability and progression.
papers.abstract: Early identification of vulnerable carotid plaques is crucial for stroke prevention, but the upstream metabolic processes linked to endothelial transition and immune recruitment remain poorly defined. We characterised lactate metabolism in ACKR1+ endothelial cells (ECs) in human carotid plaques and derived a machine-learning signature for discriminating plaque vulnerability.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with machine learning to characterize lactate metabolism in ACKR1+ endothelial cells within human carotid plaques, linking these metabolic processes to endothelial transition and immune cell recruitment. The authors derive a machine-learning signature that can discriminate vulnerable carotid plaques, potentially aiding in early stroke risk identification.

papers.title: Intranasal HSV‑1 infection drives region‑specific interferon‑dominant microglial remodeling.
papers.abstract: Herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) is a neurotropic pathogen capable of invading the central nervous system (CNS) and is associated with chronic neuroinflammation, cognitive impairment, and neurodegenerative disease. While microglia orchestrate the initial immune response to HSV‑1, the molecular mechanisms that regulate their sustained neuroinflammatory activity in vivo remain poorly understood. To define the transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms that shape microglial responses during acute HSV-1 infection in vivo, we have, for the first time, integrated single‑nucleus RNA sequencing, chr
papers.summary: This study uses single-nucleus RNA sequencing combined with chromatin accessibility profiling to map how microglia in different brain regions respond to intranasal HSV-1 infection. The authors find that infection triggers region-specific microglial remodeling dominated by interferon signaling, revealing transcriptional and epigenetic programs underlying sustained neuroinflammation. This provides a resource for understanding how HSV-1 may contribute to chronic neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative disease.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics profiling across tissue boundaries in the developing mouse brain.
papers.abstract: Tissue boundaries preserve structural integrity and guide cell differentiation during development, despite constant stress from proliferation, cell death, and tissue deformation. To study gene regulation in these regions we developed REBOSEP, a workflow for analyzing spatial transcriptomics data to detect tissue boundaries and measure gene expression relative to boundary distance. REBOSEP uses hierarchical clustering to uncover shared regulatory patterns among genes, revealing highly diverse expression changes that can shift sharply across just a few cell layers. Using this approach, the study
papers.summary: The authors developed REBOSEP, a computational workflow for spatial transcriptomics data that detects tissue boundaries and measures gene expression as a function of distance from those boundaries. Applying it to the developing mouse brain, they used hierarchical clustering to reveal that gene expression changes can be highly diverse and shift sharply across just a few cell layers near boundaries. This provides a general framework for studying gene regulation in boundary regions during development.

papers.title: Patient classification using single-cell RNA-sequencing data with deep learning convolutional neural networks.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables gene expression profiling at the resolution of individual cells, revealing cellular heterogeneity that is obscured in bulk RNA-seq. While this offers a powerful lens to study disease-specific changes, leveraging scRNA-seq data for patient phenotype classification remains challenging due to limited sample numbers, cell count variability, high dimensionality, and dependence on cell-type annotations. Existing tools attempt to address these issues using probabilistic models or attention mechanisms, but face limitations in scalability, interpretability
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning convolutional neural network approach for classifying patient phenotypes directly from single-cell RNA-sequencing data. The method aims to overcome common challenges such as limited sample sizes, variable cell counts, high dimensionality, and reliance on cell-type annotations, offering a potentially more scalable and interpretable alternative to existing probabilistic or attention-based tools.

papers.title: FDX1 is associated with CALR abundance and JAK-STAT-related inflammatory signaling in myeloproliferative neoplasms.
papers.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are driven by constitutive cytokine-receptor signaling, yet the metabolic programs associated with driver genotype and inflammatory remodeling remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study examines how the metabolic protein FDX1 relates to calreticulin (CALR) levels and JAK-STAT inflammatory signaling in myeloproliferative neoplasms. It links a metabolic factor to driver-genotype-associated inflammatory remodeling, suggesting FDX1 as a potential node connecting metabolism and cytokine signaling in MPNs.

papers.title: Integrative computational analysis of public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and CE(20:4) in colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: The fecal lipidomic changes underlying the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely characterized, particularly regarding the continuous metabolic trajectory and heterogeneity of precancerous adenomas. We aimed to use publicly available multi-omics data and an integrative computational framework to identify candidate lipidomic features associated with a CRC-like metabolic state in adenomas.
papers.summary: This study integrates public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets to identify candidate associations between the COX-2 pathway and the cholesteryl ester CE(20:4) along the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression sequence. Using computational analysis, the authors propose that this lipid feature may mark a CRC-like metabolic state in precancerous adenomas. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood identifies NETosis-associated programs and a stratified adaptive immune suppression pattern in severe acute pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with persistent organ failure and substantial mortality, yet the transcriptomic mechanisms underlying progression from mild acute pancreatitis to severe-spectrum disease remain incompletely defined. Early identification of patients at risk of persistent organ failure remains an important unmet clinical need.
papers.summary: This study integrates peripheral blood transcriptomic datasets to identify NETosis-associated gene programs that distinguish severe acute pancreatitis from mild disease. It further describes a stratified pattern of adaptive immune suppression in severe cases, suggesting blood-based signatures could help identify patients at risk of persistent organ failure.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: scLTF introduces a self-training clustering framework that combines a fast Louvain algorithm for preliminary clustering with a Transformer-based model to refine clusters on large-scale scRNA-seq data. The approach aims to overcome performance bottlenecks of existing clustering methods when applied to very large single-cell datasets. It offers a scalable alternative for cell-type identification in high-throughput experiments.

papers.title: HEXB as a Candidate Target Gene in Keloid Radiotherapy: Based on Multi-Omics Analysis and Mendelian Randomization.
papers.abstract: Keloid is a common and treatment-refractory conditions in plastic surgery and dermatology. Although radiotherapy for keloid has attracted increasing attention in recent years, its mechanism at the genetic level remains poorly characterized. This study investigated the relationship between radiation-related genes (RRGs) and keloid through an integrated multi-omics and machine learning framework, and to explore potential therapeutic agents targeting the identified key gene.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with Mendelian randomization and machine learning to identify HEXB as a candidate gene linking radiation-related pathways to keloid formation. The authors propose HEXB as a potential therapeutic target for keloid radiotherapy, though the evidence is primarily computational and associative. The work highlights a genetic angle on why radiotherapy may or may not work in keloids.

papers.title: Mapping the hepatic neural niche: from three-dimensional innervation architecture to periportal interoception and human translation.
papers.abstract: The liver has traditionally been viewed as an organ regulated by circulating hormones and long-range autonomic reflexes, with its intrahepatic neural architecture receiving comparatively little systematic attention. However, recent advances in tissue clearing, three-dimensional (3D) volumetric imaging, neural tracing, and spatial omics are reshaping this view. Here we synthesize emerging evidence that the hepatic nervous system is organized around spatially defined neurovascular-cellular niches, and propose the periportal region as a dominant anatomical site for interoceptive integration, whil
papers.summary: This review synthesizes emerging evidence that the liver contains spatially organized neurovascular-cellular niches, with the periportal region proposed as a key site for interoceptive integration. Advances in tissue clearing, 3D imaging, neural tracing, and spatial omics are reshaping the view of hepatic innervation beyond classical hormonal and autonomic regulation. The authors also discuss translation of these findings to human liver biology.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing combined with artificial intelligence to uncover immunotherapy biomarkers and decipher drug resistance mechanisms in glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma represents the most aggressive primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system, characterized by extensive intratumoral heterogeneity, profound immunosuppression, therapeutic resistance, and poor clinical outcomes. Although immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer treatment, its clinical efficacy in GBM remains limited, largely due to the complexity of the tumor ecosystem and the lack of validated predictive biomarkers. Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based computational approaches have provi
papers.summary: This review discusses how single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and AI-based computational methods can be combined to identify immunotherapy biomarkers and understand drug resistance mechanisms in glioblastoma. It highlights that GBM's intratumoral heterogeneity and immunosuppressive microenvironment limit immunotherapy efficacy, and argues that these high-resolution technologies can reveal the cellular and molecular features underlying resistance.

papers.title: From density to spatial function: spatial multi-omics, composite biomarker design, and therapeutic engineering of tertiary lymphoid structures in solid tumors.
papers.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) have emerged as clinically relevant immune niches associated with improved survival and enhanced response to immune checkpoint inhibitors across multiple solid tumors. However, translational evaluation remains dominated by density-based scoring, which inadequately captures the functional heterogeneity of histologically similar lymphoid aggregates. This review synthesizes recent advances in spatial biology that support a shift from counting TLSs to interpreting them as spatially organized immune microenvironmental units embedded within local tumor ecosystems.
papers.summary: This review argues that simply counting tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in tumors is insufficient because histologically similar aggregates can differ functionally. It synthesizes spatial biology advances—spatial multi-omics, composite biomarker design, and therapeutic engineering—to reframe TLSs as spatially organized immune microenvironmental units. The key message is that functional, spatially resolved TLS assessment could improve their use as biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis reveals a membrane tension signature associated with tumor-stroma crosstalk in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Dysregulated membrane tension (MT) drives tumor cell migration, invasion, and immune evasion, yet the prognostic value of MT-related genes (MTRGs) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to define a membrane tension-related gene signature in hepatocellular carcinoma and links it to tumor-stroma crosstalk and prognosis. The authors propose that dysregulated membrane tension genes contribute to tumor progression and immune interactions, offering a potential prognostic tool. The work is largely correlative and requires experimental validation.

papers.title: An entosis-informed prognostic index for survival stratification and molecular characterization in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Entosis is an actomyosin-dependent cell-in-cell process that may culminate in lysosome-mediated entotic cell death and is implicated in tumor evolution. Its clinical relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study constructs a prognostic index for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes related to entosis, a cell-in-cell process implicated in tumor evolution. The index is used to stratify patients by survival and to characterize the molecular features associated with different risk groups. It suggests that entosis-related gene signatures may have clinical utility for prognostication in LUAD.

papers.title: GART expression is associated with a proliferative and purine-metabolic ISC-like epithelial state in ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: To characterize the epithelial state associated with GART expression in ulcerative colitis (UC) and determine whether this association reflects a GART-specific program or a broader proliferative and purine-metabolic phenotype.
papers.summary: This study examines ulcerative colitis (UC) epithelial cells to determine whether GART expression marks a distinct epithelial state or simply reflects a general proliferative and purine-metabolic program. The authors find that GART expression is associated with an intestinal stem cell (ISC)-like epithelial state characterized by proliferation and purine metabolism, suggesting this phenotype is not GART-specific but part of a broader activation program in UC.

papers.title: Continuous spatially informed microenvironment programs show cross-cohort concordance and context-dependent spatial organization in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics resolves tissue organization in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), whereas most clinically annotated cohorts remain bulk transcriptomic datasets.
papers.summary: The authors introduce a method for deriving continuous, spatially informed microenvironment programs from spatial transcriptomics data and show that these programs are concordant across independent DLBCL cohorts. They further demonstrate that the spatial organization of these programs is context-dependent, suggesting that bulk transcriptomic cohorts can be leveraged to infer spatial microenvironment features.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies CCDC69 as a marker associated with germinal center B-cell infiltration in TNBC: development and validation.
papers.abstract: Although coiled-coil domain containing 69 (CCDC69) has been implicated in tumor biology, its role in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and immune regulation remains unclear. Bulk transcriptomic data, single-cell RNA sequencing datasets, and spatial transcriptomics were used to investigate the role of CCDC69 in TNBC. Germinal center B-cell (GCB) signatures were quantified using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA), and their associations with CCDC69 expression were assessed using correlation, ROC, and logistic regression analyses. An independent external TNBC cohort (GSE58812)
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of medical and biological research = Revista brasileira de pesquisas medicas e biologicas
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA-seq, and spatial transcriptomics to show that CCDC69 expression in triple-negative breast cancer is associated with germinal center B-cell infiltration. The authors validate CCDC69 as a potential marker linked to immune cell infiltration using correlation, ROC, and logistic regression analyses in an external TNBC cohort. The work suggests CCDC69 may serve as a biomarker for immune-related features in TNBC.

papers.title: Loss of CLIC3 in CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes is associated with immune dysfunction and poor prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the most common histological subtype of lung cancer, with a dismal prognosis partly attributed to immune evasion mediated by T cell dysfunction within the tumor microenvironment. However, the molecular determinants governing CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte functional competence remain incompletely understood. Chloride intracellular channel 3 (CLIC3) has been implicated in cancer progression, but its role in T cell immunity within the LUAD TME is unknown.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of CLIC3, a chloride channel protein, in CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes within the lung adenocarcinoma tumor microenvironment. The authors find that loss of CLIC3 in these T cells is associated with immune dysfunction and poor patient prognosis, suggesting CLIC3 may be a determinant of T cell functional competence. The work highlights a potential link between ion channel biology and anti-tumor immunity in LUAD.

papers.title: Integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with spatial analysis identifies candidate hub genes and inferred regulatory programs in atopic dermatitis.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a common chronic inflammatory disorder of the skin. Despite the availability of targeted biologics like dupilumab, heterogeneous treatment responses persist, highlighting the need for reliable biomarkers and a deeper understanding of cell-type-associated molecular programs within the tissue microenvironment.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with spatial analysis to identify candidate hub genes and infer regulatory programs in atopic dermatitis skin. The authors aim to uncover cell-type-associated molecular programs within the tissue microenvironment that may explain heterogeneous responses to biologics like dupilumab. The work nominates candidate biomarkers and regulatory networks for further validation.

papers.title: Genetic evidence and multi-omics characterization of DEHP-relevant detoxification and metabolic heterogeneity in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Human evidence linking di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) exposure to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited, and it remains unclear whether DEHP-relevant detoxification biology captures clinically meaningful HCC heterogeneity.
papers.summary: This study uses genetic and multi-omics data to investigate whether DEHP (a common phthalate plasticizer) exposure and detoxification biology are linked to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) heterogeneity. It finds evidence that DEHP-relevant detoxification pathways capture clinically meaningful variation among HCC tumors, suggesting an environmental exposure component to HCC biology.

papers.title: Cellular, chromatin-accessibility, and spatial contextualization of bulk transcriptional patterns linked to positive peritoneal cytology in endometrial cancer.
papers.abstract: Positive peritoneal cytology (PPC) identifies a clinically adverse subset of endometrial cancer, but the tumor transcriptional patterns accompanying PPC and their cellular origins remain incompletely resolved. We evaluated PPC-linked bulk RNA patterns in TCGA-UCEC and contextualized the resulting programs using independent single-cell, chromatin-accessibility, and spatial datasets.
papers.summary: This study links bulk RNA expression patterns associated with positive peritoneal cytology (PPC) in endometrial cancer to specific cell types and chromatin states using single-cell, chromatin-accessibility, and spatial datasets. By contextualizing TCGA-UCEC bulk transcriptomic signals, the authors identify cellular origins and regulatory programs underlying the adverse PPC phenotype. The work demonstrates how bulk-derived signatures can be resolved into interpretable cellular and spatial contexts.
